title: Demo · NDPS small quantity, Hindi FIR, grounds of arrest only oral
story: Accused-1, a 22-year-old student, is charged under NDPS 21(a) for 4 grams of heroin, a small quantity, so the s.37 bar does not apply; the FIR is in Hindi. He was arrested on 02.07.2026 and told the grounds of arrest only orally; the charge sheet was filed in time (day 54 of 60). The Rights Radar reads the maximum of the charged clause as one year: default bail is WINDOW_CLOSED (the charge sheet came inside the 60 days) and the BNSS s.479 undertrial limit is ELIGIBLE (136 days in custody against a threshold of 122 for a first-time offender).

steps.title: Rights Radar
steps.caption: At intake Peshkar ran the 7 rules of the Rights Radar on the dossier as of 2026-11-15: date arithmetic and statute tables, not the language model. Default bail: WINDOW_CLOSED, Undertrial limit (BNSS s.479): ELIGIBLE, Production within 24 hours: CHECK and Antil category: C. Each result names its rule and the dates it used; rules not yet re-checked against the bare act are marked unverified.

filled.label: Default bail
filled.value: WINDOW_CLOSED: 60-day limit (maximum 1 year). Day 1 is the first remand, 03.07.2026. The charge sheet was filed on day 54 (25.08.2026). It came within the limit, so the right to default bail never arose.

filled.label: Undertrial limit (BNSS s.479)
filled.value: ELIGIBLE: 136 days in custody. The threshold is 122 days for a first-time offender (1/3 of 1 years, on bond) and 183 days otherwise (1/2, on bail). The applicable threshold (1/3, first-time offender) of 122 days has been reached. The record shows no other pending case (BNSS s.479(2)).

filled.label: Antil category
filled.value: C: Charged under a special act with stringent bail provisions (NDPS s.37): category C. Antil's categories decide how an accused who was not arrested during investigation and cooperated is treated after the charge sheet; for a client in custody this is context, not a bail entitlement.

filled.label: Statutory bar
filled.value: NOT_APPLICABLE: The NDPS section charged is a small-quantity clause, which NDPS s.37(1)(b) does not reach.

steps.title: Abhiyojak argues the other side
steps.caption: Abhiyojak, the prosecution sparring partner, raised 6 objections in 2 rounds, each grounded in a prosecution argument from comparable orders or a fact of the case; 3 ungrounded objections were discarded. Abhiyojak judged 0 of Vakeel's replies: 0 answered, 0 partly answered, 0 unanswered; 6 objections could not be judged because the sparring token budget was spent, and stay unanswered. Whatever stays open is listed at Gate 2, and counsel answers it before approving.

filled.value: UNANSWERED: The applicant is charged under NDPS 21(a), which involves a serious offence under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, warranting continued judicial scrutiny of custodial necessity.

filled.label: O2 against general (gravity and punishment)
filled.value: UNANSWERED: The offence under NDPS 21(a) carries a maximum punishment of one year, but the prosecution opposes bail on the ground of gravity and severity of punishment, as reflected in the charge sheet and the nature of the accusation.

filled.label: O3 against general (flight risk)
filled.value: UNANSWERED: The prosecution opposes bail on the ground that the applicant is a flight risk, as the applicant is named in the charge sheet and the warrant of arrest is pending, raising apprehension of absconding.

filled.label: O4 against general (witness tampering)
filled.value: UNANSWERED: The prosecution opposes bail on the ground of reasonable apprehension of tampering with prosecution witnesses, as the trial is at a conclusive end with eleven witnesses examined to date.

filled.label: O5 against general (antecedents)
filled.value: UNANSWERED: The prosecution opposes bail on the ground of bad antecedents, as the applicant is named in the FIR and the prosecution witnesses have reiterated their version as alleged in the FIR.

filled.label: O6 against general (statutory bar)
filled.value: UNANSWERED: The prosecution opposes bail on the ground of statutory bar under Section 37(1) of the NDPS Act, as the offence involves commercial quantity and the court cannot record satisfaction that there are reasonable grounds for believing the applicant is not guilty.
